    @staticmethod
    def _transition_property_rank(name):
        """Rank a transition property section by how canonical its intensities are.

        A single ORCA output usually contains several tables describing the
        intensities of the same electronic transitions, since ORCA prints the
        spectrum in more than one representation (for example both "via
        transition electric dipole moments" and "via transition velocity dipole
        moments" for TDDFT), optionally supplemented by multipole corrected,
        spin-orbit corrected or core level (X-ray) spectra.  All of these
        tables are exported through the ORCA specific transprop attribute, but
        etenergies/etoscs can only hold one spectrum, so the sections are
        ranked here and only the most meaningful one is used for them.

        The rank is a tuple of flags meant for lexicographic comparison, where
        a larger rank marks a section that is a better source of the exported
        oscillator strengths.  It is derived from the printed section title
        alone, so it also covers titles which need no special table parsing
        (extra qualifiers such as "(origin adjusted)", emission spectra, ...)
        and it does not depend on the order in which ORCA prints the sections.
        """
        title = name.upper()
        return (
            # cclib exposes the valence electronic transitions, with
            # etenergies in wavenumbers.  X-ray sections instead list core
            # level transitions, with energies in eV and normalized
            # intensities rather than oscillator strengths.
            'X-RAY' not in title,
            # Oscillator strengths of an absorption spectrum; the same states
            # can additionally be printed as an emission spectrum.
            'EMISSION' not in title,
            # Spin-orbit corrected spectra refer to the spin-mixed states,
            # which are a different (and longer) list of states than the
            # spin-free ones parsed into etenergies, etsecs and etsyms.
            'SPIN ORBIT' not in title and 'SOC ' not in title,
            # Oscillator strengths are conventionally reported in the length
            # representation, i.e. via the transition electric dipole moments.
            # The velocity representation is an alternative gauge which only
            # coincides with the length one in the basis set limit, so it must
            # not shadow the electric dipole values.
            'VELOCITY' not in title,
            # The combined spectra add magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole
            # contributions to the electric dipole intensity, so their
            # intensity column is not the electric dipole oscillator strength.
            'QUADRUPOLE' not in title,
        )

    fosc = 2/3 * dE[au] * T2[au**2]
while the velocity table obeys
    fosc = 2/3 * P2[au**2] / dE[au].
Both relations are used to decide which representation the exported etoscs
values belong to.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import io, logging, re, sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "source"))
import numpy
from cclib.parser.orcaparser import ORCA

CM_TO_AU = 1.0 / 219474.6313702


def parse(path):
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    p = ORCA(io.StringIO(text), loglevel=logging.WARNING)
    p.metadata["package_version"] = "4.2.0"
    stream = iter(io.StringIO(text))
    try:
        for line in stream:
            p.extract(stream, line)
    except StopIteration:
        pass
    return p


def tables(text):
    """Return {title: rows} for every 'State Energy Wavelength fosc T2 ...' table."""
    out = {}
    lines = text.splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        title = line.strip()
        if "ABSORPTION SPECTRUM VIA TRANSITION" not in title:
            continue
        rows = []
        for row in lines[i + 4:]:
            fields = row.split()
            if len(fields) != 8:
                break
            rows.append([float(f) for f in fields])
        out[title] = numpy.array(rows)
    return out


def check(path):
    p = parse(path)
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    etoscs = numpy.asarray(p.etoscs, dtype=float)
    etenergies = numpy.asarray(p.etenergies, dtype=float)
    ok = True
    print(f"--- {path.name}")
    for title, rows in tables(text).items():
        energy, fosc, sq = rows[:, 1], rows[:, 3], rows[:, 4]
        de = energy * CM_TO_AU
        predicted = 2.0 / 3.0 * de * sq if "ELECTRIC" in title else 2.0 / 3.0 * sq / de
        gauge = "length" if "ELECTRIC" in title else "velocity"
        print(f"    {gauge:9s} table self-consistent: "
              f"{numpy.allclose(predicted, fosc, rtol=2e-2, atol=1e-6)}")
        same = etoscs.shape == fosc.shape and numpy.allclose(etoscs, fosc)
        print(f"    etoscs == {gauge} fosc column: {same}")
        if gauge == "length" and not same:
            ok = False
        if gauge == "velocity" and same:
            ok = False
    # energies must be paired with the intensities and use wavenumbers
    print(f"    len(etoscs) == len(etenergies): {etoscs.size == etenergies.size}")
    ok = ok and etoscs.size == etenergies.size
    # sanity: exported etoscs must reproduce the length-gauge relation with the
    # exported energies
    lengths = [t for t in tables(text) if "ELECTRIC" in t]
    if lengths:
        rows = tables(text)[lengths[0]]
        pred = 2.0 / 3.0 * (etenergies * CM_TO_AU) * rows[:, 4]
        consistent = numpy.allclose(pred, etoscs, rtol=2e-2, atol=1e-6)
        print(f"    etoscs == 2/3 dE T2 from exported etenergies: {consistent}")
        ok = ok and consistent
    print(f"    => {'CONSISTENT' if ok else 'INCONSISTENT'}")
    return ok


paths = [ROOT / "fixtures" / "public_orca_spectrum.out"]
paths += sorted((Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "cases").glob("*.out"))
paths += sorted((Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "cases2").glob("*.out"))
